text:
maya: Heads up — ran the quickstart tarball on WSL2 and the installer created a folder named '~/.redwood' (literal tilde, with quotes). localserve/localtest couldn't find profiles and auth login failed. Has anyone seen the installer write unexpanded tildes?

joel: yikes. which install command did you run? and `redwoodctl --version`?

maya: I did `sudo ./install.sh --prefix /opt/redwood` because I wanted a system install. redwoodctl 0.12.3.

joel: sudo can change HOME, but creating a quoted '~/.redwood' suggests the script wrote the literal string or used single quotes that never got expanded. can you paste `ls -la /opt/redwood`?

maya: pasted this in the shell:```
/opt/redwood$ ls -la
drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 4096 Mar 2 10:12 '.'
drwxr-xr-x 12 root root 4096 Mar 2 09:58 '..'
drwxr-xr-x 3 1000 1000 4096 Mar 2 10:12 '~/.redwood'
```

samir: yeah that's the literal-dir case. quickfix: move it into your real home and fix perms:```
sudo mv /opt/redwood/'~/.redwood' $HOME/.redwood || sudo mv "~/.redwood" $HOME/.redwood
sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.redwood
```
That should restore profile discovery.

maya: moved it, profile lookup works now, but `redwoodctl auth login` opens the browser and the callback returns 400 `redirect_uri_mismatch`. I started localserve on port 8086.

devex-bot: Known issue #452: installer writes local OAuth client redirect to http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback. CLI `localserve --port` flag is not propagated to the saved client redirect. Workaround documented in #452.

joel: installer defaults to 8080 for the redirect. two options: run localserve on 8080, or recreate/update the local client with the correct redirect URI.

samir: to replace the client file quickly:```
redwoodctl auth create-client --name local-dev --redirect http://127.0.0.1:8086/callback
# then replace $HOME/.redwood/client.json with the new client info or point localserve to the client via REDWOOD_CLIENT_FILE env var
```
Note: `auth create-client` prints id/secret — treat it like secrets.

maya: created a new client and swapped the file, login succeeded. I'll open a PR to: (1) make the installer always expand tilde (no literal quotes), (2) make the installer honor a LOCALSERVE_PORT env var/write the redirect to match `localserve --port`, and (3) add an e2e test that runs the installer under sudo and checks no path contains a literal tilde and that redirect uri uses the configured port.

joel: add a regression test for `redwoodctl install --noninteractive` too. also include exact repro steps and the ls output.

samir: assigning issue to @maya, label `needs-e2e` and cc devex. thanks for the clear repro. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — will ping for review when PR is up.
